title: A consumer override of a generated stage skill wins over the packaged skill, tracks edits, and reverts when removed
statement: In an isolated trusted project whose `.pi/settings.json` holds Kiln's package entry and the skill-override entry `../planning-content/skills-overrides` as produced by `mergeSettingsText`, the pinned Pi runtime's real resource loader, reloaded for each state, resolves the generated skill identity `kiln-stage-01-intake` exactly as follows. (1) Packaged only - the override directory exists and holds no skill: the loaded skill's `filePath` is the packaged `pi-package/skills/kiln-stage-01-intake/SKILL.md`, and Pi reports no collision for that identity. (2) Override present - `planning-content/skills-overrides/kiln-stage-01-intake/SKILL.md` declares that name: exactly one skill with that identity loads, its `filePath` is the override file, and Pi's collision diagnostic names the override file as the winner path and the packaged file as the loser path. (3) Override edited - the override's description is changed: the same override `filePath` loads, with the edited description. (4) Override skill removed while the override directory and the settings entry remain: the packaged `filePath` and the packaged description load again, and Pi reports no collision for that identity. In every state the other packaged skills still load from the package. Provenance is read from `filePath` and the collision diagnostic's winner and loser paths, never from model behaviour. Pi 0.84.4 resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources, and the first skill loaded with a given identity wins, so this criterion claims only that the consumer override wins over the packaged skill, not over every earlier project-settings skill path.
notes: ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (F91, F92). The criterion said the override directory was registered after the packaged set, and it named three states. Pi 0.84.4 resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources and keeps the first skill with each name, and TSK-0047 promises four states; the packaged-only state and the exact meaning of removal - the skill removed, the directory and the entry kept - are now stated, with one generated identity and path-based provenance. ⚠️ CONTROLS, RECORDED AS BEHAVIOUR (D9). An absent override directory is silently ignored: Pi skips a settings skill path that does not exist, emits no diagnostic, and the packaged skill loads. An untrusted project - no trust decision, or an explicit denial - loads neither the package's resources nor the override, because Pi empties project settings when the project is not trusted. Neither control is a Kiln refusal. ⚠️ R8, NOT CLAIMED. Kiln's settings merge keeps every existing project `skills` entry where it is and appends its own. Project-settings entries share Pi's precedence and keep their order, so an earlier project-settings skill path holding the same identity outranks Kiln's appended override entry. This criterion does not claim otherwise. ⚠️ R9 IS SETUP'S (TSK-0060). The entry is fixed relative to `.pi`; that it names the selected content root's `skills-overrides/` is for setup to guarantee. This criterion proves the entry in the default layout, where the content root is `<project>/planning-content`.
